summary: Modern databases and data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML capabilities directly where data lives, eliminating the need for separate model servers or vector stores. Capabilities range from in-database LLM inference and SQL-callable ML functions (Snowflake Cortex, BigQuery ML, Redshift ML, Aurora ML) to native vector search for retrieval-augmented generation (Databricks, MongoDB Atlas). For organizations with existing PostgreSQL infrastructure, extensions like pgvector and pgai add embedding storage and semantic search without adopting a dedicated vector database, which Gartner projects 30% of enterprises will rely on for GenAI workloads by 2026.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.description: Cortex provides serverless, SQL- and Python-callable LLM functions (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EXTRACT_ANSWER), Cortex Search for hybrid semantic/keyword retrieval, Cortex Analyst for natural-language-to-SQL, and Cortex Agents. Models from Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, and others are hosted within Snowflake's governance boundary.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake offers a VECTOR data type with VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY / VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE functions, plus the fully managed Cortex Search service for hybrid vector + keyword retrieval.
databases.llm_integration: Built-in hosted LLMs (Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic, OpenAI via partnerships) callable directly from SQL/Python; no external API keys required.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing in Snowflake credits; Cortex LLM functions billed per million tokens by model, Cortex Search billed on serving compute plus storage.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets you create and run ML models using standard SQL (regression, classification, clustering, time-series, matrix factorization) and invoke remote Vertex AI models, including Gemini, for generative tasks via ML.GENERATE_TEXT, ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, and AI.GENERATE functions directly over warehouse data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery provides the VECTOR_SEARCH function and CREATE VECTOR INDEX for approximate nearest-neighbor search over embedding columns.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI and Gemini models via remote model connections; embeddings and text generation callable from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery on-demand (per TB scanned) or capacity-based slot pricing; generative and embedding functions incur additional Vertex AI model inference charges.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: Open-source PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities through extensions: pgvector adds a vector column type and similarity operators, while pgai (from Timescale) adds in-database embedding creation and LLM calls (OpenAI, Ollama, Anthropic) via SQL functions, letting teams keep relational data, embeddings, and AI workflows in one engine.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to core PostgreSQL. Vector search is provided by the third-party pgvector extension, which adds the vector type and HNSW/IVFFlat indexes; it must be installed and enabled separately.
databases.llm_integration: Via pgai, which exposes SQL functions to generate embeddings and call hosted LLMs; otherwise LLM calls are handled in the application layer.
databases.pricing_notes: PostgreSQL and both extensions are free/open-source; cost is driven by self-managed or cloud-hosted compute/storage plus any external LLM API usage.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you add ML-based predictions to applications using SQL by integrating Aurora (MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible) with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock. SQL queries can invoke deployed models for inference and call Bedrock foundation models for generative tasks and embeddings.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native. Aurora ML itself does not provide vector search; vector storage/search on Aurora PostgreSQL requires the pgvector extension, which is a separate capability from Aurora ML.
databases.llm_integration: SQL-level integration with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker-hosted models for inference and embedding generation.
databases.pricing_notes: Standard Aurora compute/storage/I-O pricing; ML inference adds SageMaker endpoint or Bedrock model invocation charges.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.description: Redshift ML enables data analysts and engineers to create, train, and deploy ML models using familiar SQL commands (CREATE MODEL), with training delegated to Amazon SageMaker Autopilot. It supports in-warehouse prediction functions and integration with Amazon Bedrock for generative AI over warehouse data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native. Redshift ML focuses on SQL-based model training and inference; it does not provide a built-in vector index or ANN search function as a core Redshift ML feature.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock for LLM-based generation and with SageMaker for custom model inference, invoked from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift compute/storage pricing (RA3 nodes or Serverless RPUs); model training/inference incurs additional SageMaker or Bedrock charges.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.description: Databricks Mosaic AI provides end-to-end tooling for building, fine-tuning, serving, and governing ML and generative AI models, including Model Serving, Agent Framework, and foundation model APIs. Databricks Vector Search is a managed service that automatically syncs and indexes embeddings from Delta tables for retrieval.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a fully managed, built-in vector database that creates and auto-syncs indexes from Delta tables and supports hybrid (vector + keyword) search.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Model Serving and Foundation Model APIs provide access to proprietary and open models (Llama, DBRX, external providers like OpenAI/Anthropic) with an agent framework for RAG.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs); Vector Search and Model Serving billed on compute/serving units plus underlying cloud infrastructure.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search lets you store vector embeddings alongside operational document data and run semantic similarity queries using the aggregation pipeline ($vectorSearch stage). It supports approximate nearest-neighbor search with filtering and combines with Atlas Search for hybrid full-text plus vector retrieval.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Atlas Vector Search is a built-in capability of MongoDB Atlas, providing vector indexes and the $vectorSearch aggregation stage integrated with the document model.
databases.llm_integration: No hosted LLMs; integrates with external providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Hugging Face, Bedrock, Vertex) and frameworks like LangChain/LlamaIndex for embedding generation and RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Available on Atlas managed clusters; vector search runs on cluster or dedicated Search Node compute, billed as part of Atlas consumption/instance pricing.
